analysis.title: Sell low, buy high
key_insights: NVDA surged 30% and SOX rose 14% in a violent reversal of the AI complex, following heavy hedge fund de-risking and a collapse in semiconductor valuations.
NDX single-day rallies above 5% are rare over 15+ years (April 2025, November 2022, March 2020, December 2018), and all occurred at or near major market lows per Callahan.
The Market Ear flagged the NDX 2018 analogy before the move. The analogy suggests more upside could follow before another leg lower.
SOX forward P/E fell to 12-13x, effectively a 15-year low, while semiconductor earnings revisions remain positive (Callahan, pre-squeeze).
The semiconductor selloff is multiple compression rather than falling profits, as SOX earnings estimates stay near record highs.

GS PB shows hedge funds cutting risk aggressively: US single-stock shorting at the highest weekly level since June 2022 and third highest in a decade. ETF shorts rose 11% in one week. Data runs through Thursday and misses Friday's selling.
Fundamental L/S net leverage dropped to 42.3%, 1st percentile over the past year. Beta-adjusted net leverage fell more than 22 points since early October to 48.2%, a five-year low.
JPM PI shows the decline from 12m highs in positioning is in line with the most extreme episodes since 2018.
Short gamma risks magnifying market moves in both directions.
Memory stocks led North Asia selling, contributing to an eighth consecutive week of tech selling. Asia fundamental L/S net leverage is at record lows.
Gold volatility spiked massively on Friday alongside falling spot, the most violent such move since the March bubble burst.

market_movers.rationale: NVDA exploded 30% in a squeeze after the 'Jensen news' following deep de-risking and valuation compression.

sector_views.rationale: SOX forward P/E at 12-13x, a 15-year low, with estimates near record highs. The selloff was multiple compression, and positioning was extremely washed out.

earnings_insights: SOX earnings estimates remain near record highs and semiconductor earnings revisions remain positive despite the selloff (forward estimates, not a print).
risk_factors: The 2018 analogy suggests a possible further leg lower after the furious bounce.
Short gamma can magnify moves in both directions.
GS PB data excludes Friday's selling, so the deleveraging may be understated.
